reason: Both correctly identified the blocked defrost drain, but Conversation 2 explained what and where the drain is up front so the homeowner found and cleared it in one step, then correctly confirmed the fix, gave sensible prevention advice (keep veg off the back wall, periodic flush) and reserved escalation only for genuine recurrence. Conversation 1 needed extra turns to locate the hole, then muddled things with a 'drain hose' heading and a replacement-part panel for a job that needs no part, pushed an unnecessary unplug for a cotton bud (later walked back), and ended by suggesting an engineer if it recurs rather than checking the tube/tray first. Conversation 2's mention of stiff wire is a minor caution against the sharp-tool boundary, but it never approached the back wall and the warm-water-only guidance dominated, so it still served the homeowner better overall.
